newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 182nd 10-yr JGB yield hits record low 2.065%.
newsitem.headline: Key 182nd 10-yr JGB yield hits record low 2.065%.

text.p: The key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) yield fell to 2.065 percent, an all-time record low for any benchmark 10-year JGB, on Friday morning, traders said.
The yield closed at 2.075 percent on Thursday.

The bond yield fell in reaction to price rises in the key September JGB futures contract, which was buoyed by dealers' short-covering ahead of a shift in benchmark to the December contract later this month, traders said.
The September was at 127.04 at 0119 GMT, up 0.07 from Thursday's close.
"The number of participants was limited in the middle of summer holiday season. Nobody was in hurry with buying (cash bonds)," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said they will focus on Tokyo July department store sales data, due out at 0530 GMT, and Japan's revised industrial output data for June at 0430 GMT.
"The data for both is expected to be weak. If they are stronger than expected, the September may fall by 0.20-0.30 yen," the dealer said.
